newsitem.title: USA: Appliance Recycling Q2 might show profit.
newsitem.headline: Appliance Recycling Q2 might show profit.

text.p: Appliance Recycling Centers of America Inc said Wednesday it expects results from near-breakeven to a small profit in this year's second quarter.
The quarter should benefit from an improved outlook for recycled appliance sales and lower expenses.
Earlier today, the company reported 1997 first quarter earnings of $63,000 or $0.06 per share, a turnaround from the net loss of $1.98 million or $1.75 in the year-earlier period.
Revenues totaled $3.2 million, up from $3.06 million in the first quarter of 1996.

Edward Cameron, president and chief executive officer, said the 1997 first quarter earnings turnaround was due to above-plan sales of its Encore reconditioned appliances and significantly lower operating expenses.
He said first quarter results also benefited from strong levels of recycling volumes in support of the energy conservation program of Southern California Edison Co.

Cameron said the restructuring last year of its Encore division allows the company to manage more effectively its 14 remaining retail outlets. The company closed three recycling centers and 12 retail stores in the restructuring.

Same-store Encore sales (a sales comparison among the six stores open in the first quarters of 1997 and 1996) increased 23 percent. Total Encore sales rose 12 percent in the first quarter, which also exceeded internal forecasts, he said.

Also as a result of the Encore restructuring, overhead and other operating expenses have been reduced, he said in a statement. Selling, general and administrative expenses fell 29 percent in the first quarter of 1997 in comparison to the year-earlier level.
Appliance Recycling is the nation's largest recycler of major household appliances.
